newsitem.title: UK: NWE high, low sulphur fuel oil strong.
newsitem.headline: NWE high, low sulphur fuel oil strong.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil was firmer on Wednesday as crude oil rose again, traders said.
High sulphur barges were firm, trading at between $113.50 and $115 fob ARA. This compares with $107-$110 on Tuesday.
High sulphur cargoes were well supported and utility players reported offers between $115 and $116 cif NWE. This follows the sale of a trader's Coryton cargo on Tuesday to a major at $114.50 cif.
Another trader's prompt Coryton cargo was heard on offer at $116, while material was also thought available out of Scandinavia and northern France.

Two high sulphur Isab cargoes were heard available in the Med and dealers said transatlantic arbitrage business was almost workable for these. The cargoes had been bought at a 50 cent premium to the quoted high fob.
Low sulphur markets were a dollar or two firmer, with swaps valued at around $128/$129 cif NWE.
Low sulphur straight-run cargo markets were thin in November. A buyer seeking barrels for early December said he had heard offers of around $150 cif NWE. But he was at least $6 lower.
